full_judgment:
6. Mr Ibrahim Mollah, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-petitioner, submits that the trial Court after hearing the parties and the deposition and considering the Exhibits since found possession of the petitioner dismissed the suit which is very much in accordance with law against which the plaintiff-appellant-opposite parties have preferred appeal and the appellate Court without discussing the evidences allowed the appeal thus occasioned failure of justice. He further submits that both the plaintiff and the defendant though claimed the property by way of pattan but no pattan was produced before the court, RS was prepared in the name of the predecessors of the plaintiff and defendant. The petitioner has purchased by 3 registered deeds (Exhibits GH) on different dates and there was mutation case being No. 174 of 1986 and has been paying rent to the Government which are marked as Exhibit A series and paid rent up to 1991 and referred 28 DLR (AD) 61 and 32 DLR 252 wherein it has been stated Record of Right is not a document of title. It does not create or extinguish title to land. At best, along with other evidence it may support evidences of title. By itself, it is not an evidence of title "and it has been referred in 32 DLR 252 that Record of Right is evidence of present possession-Registered Kabala evidence of title. The records of rights of the Government which at best are evidence of possession at the time when such records are prepared and not an evidence of title as such this is a well-established principle of law. A registered Kabala is an evidence of title which will prevail over the other records of rights as such until and unless such kabala is canceled on a specific allegation of fraud by any civil Court in an appropriate civil suit." He has further referred 43 DLR 226 "There is no specific area or demarcation of the land allegedly encroached by the defendants- opposite parties, in such a case no order of temporary injunction can be granted" and in this connection he has referred schedule 'A' description of the plaint where the boundary was not specifically mentioned and where there was no specific demarcation of the plot. The plaintiff-opposite party cannot claim for an injunction or is not entitled to have injunction. The appellate Court while disposing of the appeal did not consider this very aspect rather considered the dakhilas as produced by the plaintiff (marked as Exhibit 6) and the rent receipt to the government (marked as Exhibit 5) in this connection. He has referred 30 DLR (SC) 41 "the private document made an exhibit on its formal proof, presumption as to its writing-question of its genuineness is a question of fact" and he submits that the Exhibit 6 are all private documents and the burden of proof is on him to prove his genuineness of the rent receipts which were not at all proved. Thus the appellate Court being the final court of fact should have considered all these aspects for which he is not entitled thus occasioned an error in the decision required to be interfered by this court. 

 8. I have gone through the judgments of both the courts below and also Exhibits as filed by both the parties. Admitted fact is that the CS Khatian was prepared in the name of Jagadish and Ashutosh from where the plaintiff claims the ownership but the pattans were not produced by plaintiff and defendant before the court though RS was prepared in the name of the predecessor of the plaintiff and defendants. The plaintiff produced some dakhilas and also rent receipts i.e. Exhibit 5 which appeared to have been paid on 16-3-1980 and Exhibit 5 Ka is paid in 1969 in the name of Tayab Khan and Exhibit 6 series are the dakhilas given by the jaminder and the defendants have also filed rent receipts of the government which were marked as Exhibit A series and admitted position is that he paid rent up to 1991. The defendants have mutated and submitted some documents of that purchase deed of different dates i.e. 12-3-1979 and 5-12-1979. The dakhilas submitted by the plaintiff are the private documents and that are ie, to be proved by the scribe, the signatures are to be compared which were not considered by the lower appellate Court. These private dakhilas are yet to be proved and it is referred in 35 DLR 129 "that dakhilas are private documents and it would not carry any presumption of correctness as would be available in the case of any entry in the record of rights under the provisions of the Bengal Tenancy Act. It appears that both the parties have adduced rent receipts and the petitioner has paid rent up to 1991 and there was mutation though the mutation proceeding is under challenge in the appeal and, according to decision 35 DLR (AD) 216, rent receipts are evidence of possession, and may be used as collateral evidence of title. The petitioner has submitted certain rent receipts marked as Exhibit A series which were not considered by the learned appellate Court. Though it is a question of fact based on finding and is proved and this aspect since not discussed by the learned appellate Court, I find substance in this Rule. Since rent receipts are evidence of possession and collateral evidence of title and in a suit for permanent injunction where the plaintiff did not mention the boundary of the specific plot and there is no specific demarcation, in that view of the matter, granting injunction in favour of the plaintiff cannot be sustained.
